title: unabbreviateNumber does not work
body:
**Describe the bug**
The `unabbreviateNumber` function does not unabbreviate the abbreviated number

**To Reproduce**
```
Welcome to Node.js v22.22.0.
Type ".help" for more information.
> const { unabbreviateNumber } = require('js-abbreviation-number')
undefined
> unabbreviateNumber("10K", ["K"])
10

```
**Expected behavior**
returns 10000

**Screenshots**
```
Welcome to Node.js v22.22.0.
Type ".help" for more information.
> const { unabbreviateNumber } = require('js-abbreviation-number')
undefined
> unabbreviateNumber("10K", ["K"])
10
```
author: ryanoboril

comments.author: moh3n9595
comments.body: Thanks for the example. Custom symbols can be changed, but their positions determine their values. The first entry is the base unit (×1), so ["K"] makes K mean ×1. Use unabbreviateNumber("10K", ["", "K"]) to get 10000.
